\section{Annual walk-forward financial audit}\label{sec:financial-annual-walkforward-audit}
An outcome-blind CRSP audit selects 100 liquid endpoint-stable ETFs from 427 ETF identities, versus 25 in the terminal audit; the finite grammar has 9600 strategies. Five annual 2020--2024 decisions use trailing five-year profiles, and their top-five marginal-coverage selections are hashed before next-year targets are read. The initial analytical design preceded return extraction; amendments are disclosed separately and the adverse terminal-audit result remains unchanged.

\paragraph{Walk-forward result.} Marginal coverage averaged 0.0704, versus 0.0119 for the strongest comparator, and was positive in 3 of 5 annual episodes. Its descriptive 95\% annual-bootstrap interval was [0.0190, 0.1187]. Mean candidate-level Spearman association was 0.1279 and mean greedy-oracle regret was 0.3150; the redesign improves the registered mechanism comparison but leaves substantial ranking error.
\paragraph{Compression and decomposition.} Frontier-only pruning preserved current validation value while changing future candidate quality by -0.1020. Innovation-safe compression preserved the registered frontier, closure, and future-quality identities. The safely retained library contained 1 currently dominated carrier with positive purely generative value, illustrating why current dominance alone is not a safe deletion rule.
\paragraph{Data and claim boundary.} Licensed rows are not distributed. The universe is larger but survivorship-biased, the snapshot is not revision-timestamped, the annual lock is retrospective, five annual units give coarse uncertainty, and costs are reduced form. The exercise supports no market-alpha, ranking-consistency, or new Lean claim.
